summary: A node removed from its fleet records the removal even when the refusal arrives while it publishes its endpoints, instead of its replication worker stalling

schema.detail: No table, index, schema-version, fleet.toml or wire change: the refusal is written to the same files, under the same lock, in the same order.

rules.detail: No checkpoint, retention or digest change.

compatibility.detail: The replication worker now waits for the fleet settings lock off its async runtime. Before, a refusal that arrived while endpoint publication held that lock could stall the worker: it printed that it stops syncing and never wrote [removed] to fleet.toml.

manual.detail: No manual step. A worker that stalled this way on an earlier build records the removal at its next refusal after the upgrade restarts it.

recovery.detail: Binary swap-back is supported; an earlier build has the stall again.
